ig_caption:
If they'd poured the Hoover Dam all at once, it would have needed about 125 years to cool. 🧊 Watch 5 years of building in 26 seconds. ⏱️

First they moved the Colorado River: four 56-ft tunnels were blasted through the canyon walls and cofferdams sealed off the site. Then, from June 1933, the concrete went in as hundreds of separate blocks, raised a few feet at a time.

The twist: a single pour would have cracked as it cooled. So hundreds of miles of pipe were built into the concrete, carrying ice-cold water through it. Tests in 1995 showed the concrete is still slowly gaining strength.

Would you walk across the top? Yes or no 👇

yt_title: How the Hoover Dam Was Built: 5 Years in 26 Seconds #shorts
yt_description:
1931: contract awarded; river diverted through four 56-ft-diameter tunnels; cofferdams; excavation to bedrock. 6 June 1933: first concrete, poured in column blocks a few feet at a time with embedded cooling pipes (one continuous pour would have taken ~125 years to cool). Last concrete 29 May 1935; dedicated 30 Sep 1935; 726 ft high. 1995 cores: the concrete is still slowly gaining strength.

Sources: https://www.asce.org/about-civil-engineering/history-and-heritage/historic-landmarks/hoover-dam · https://www.nrmca.org/america250/hoover-dam/
Figures are historical estimates. Stylised 3D animation.
